CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's Q1 2026 results were undeniably strong: revenue up 22% YoY to $17.4B, EPS up 30% to $5.47, a record $63B backlog, and a raised full-year guidance to low double-digit growth. The Power & Energy segment is a genuine secular tailwind from AI data center buildouts, with power generation sales up 41%. However, the stock has already re-rated massively — P/E has expanded from ~17x a year ago to 45.5x currently, and the stock is up 170% over 12 months. At 45x diluted P/E and 23x P/B, the valuation is at the extreme top of its 365-day range and prices in substantial continued execution. Tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.4B for 2026 are real and compressing margins (operating margin 17.7% vs. prior year, Resource Industries margin collapsed to 10% from 17%). The QoQ revenue actually declined 1.3% and operating cash flow fell 50% QoQ to $1.87B. The balance sheet shows rising leverage (total liabilities up to $76.9B from $66.9B a year ago). While the fundamental trajectory is positive and the AI power generation story is credible, the valuation has run far ahead of near-term earnings power, leaving limited margin of safety. The score reflects genuinely strong fundamentals offset by an extremely stretched valuation.
key_factors: Q1 2026 revenue +22% YoY to $17.4B, EPS +30% to $5.47, beating consensus by ~20%
Record $63B backlog (+79% YoY) provides multi-year revenue visibility
Power & Energy segment: power generation sales +41% driven by AI data center demand; capacity expansion to 3x 2024 levels by 2030
P/E expanded from ~17x (May 2025) to 45.5x (May 2026) — at extreme top of 365-day range, pricing in flawless execution
Tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.4B for 2026; $710M unfavorable manufacturing costs in Q1 alone; Resource Industries margin collapsed to 10% from 17%
QoQ revenue declined 1.3% and operating cash flow fell 50% to $1.87B — some near-term normalization
Balance sheet leverage increasing: total liabilities $76.9B vs $66.9B a year ago; equity flat at $18.7B
Stock up ~170% over 12 months — significant momentum already embedded in price
Near-term catalyst: potential $1.5-1.8B tariff refund from Supreme Court IEEPA ruling could provide earnings boost
Analyst consensus 2026 EPS ~$23.99 implies forward P/E of ~38x — still premium valuation

sources_cited.excerpt: Management has guided to a substantial tariff headwind in the range of $2.2 billion to $2.4 billion for 2026... In Q1 2026 alone, approximately $710 million of unfavorable manufacturing costs were largely tariff-driven
Resource Industries segment... sales growing a modest 4% to $3.8 billion but segment profit plummeting 39% to $378 million. The segment profit margin contracted sharply to 10.0% from 17.0%

A landmark Supreme Court ruling (the IEEPA case) in February 2026 struck down several executive-imposed tariffs as unconstitutional. Analysts estimate this could result in Caterpillar receiving between $1.5 billion and $1.8 billion in retroactive tariff refunds

Power Generation sales within the segment jumped 41% to $2.817 billion... Caterpillar is aggressively expanding capacity—planning to increase large reciprocating engine production to nearly 3 times 2024 levels by 2030
